title: The fight with Leonard Feather at the Village Vanguard
summary: Carrying ten pounds of marijuana in his hat, he punched Feather on the Vanguard steps, igniting a brawl.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: One night, on my off night, on Monday night we had a jam session down in the Village VANGUARD And I had just flown in from Chicago. I went to Chicago to get some grass. Had ten pounds of grass in a paper bag sitting inside my porkpie hat on the table. Everybody thought it was my lunch. (Laughter). Well, the most obvious place is that you see it, you know it. If you hide it, someone is going to wonder what you are hiding. No one bothered it.

Now Monty Kaye and Pete Gallaran and the other partner, they used to promote jam sessions on Sundays at Kelley's Stables. They were there. So we -- You've been in the Vanguard, haven't you. You know how you step down the steps going out on the further side of the wall. You come down and walk a step

down the step. I was going to go down the steps and Leonard was coming up the steps. And I grabbed him by his arm. I say Hey man, I say when are you going to be giving me my money? He say what do you mean, I don't owe you any money. And if you want to make an ass of yourself, you do it at someone else's expense and take your hands off of me you jerk.

And when he said that, I went right up against his melon. I broke his dentures, his nose, his eye glasses. Now the waiters to the rescue. Now the cashier was Max Gordon's brother-in-law, Max Gordon, the owner of the club didn't like him. And he was paralyzed on one side. The waiter has my arms pinned behind me and the cashier is going to throw a punch at me. I say well how do you like that. To myself. So by this waiter holding my arms behind me, I just tightened up and put both feet in his chest. (Laughter). He went sailing across the room. We broke up tables, chairs, all of the whiskey. The waiters come out on the losing end as a rule, you know, the waiters win. They didn't win that night because I had my punch with me.

And on the bandstand, was Clyde Hart. He was a pretty good piano player. He always ran around with Art Tatum and smoked a cigar. He was good for chord structure. He played somewhat on the style of Teddy Wilson. He was out here with Stuff Smith's band also. Same time that Cozy Cole was with the band. I think that band, speaking of Stuff's band. He had

Bernard Addison playing guitar. Jonah Jones, Cozy, I can't remember the bass player's name and Clyde Heart. But anyway, at the Vanguard, Clyde was playing the piano, Buster Bailey playing clarinet, Charlie Shavers was playing trumpet. Ben Tharp, Ben, Ed Thigpen's father, playing drums and myself. Now they all stayed on the bandstand. Lester looked up and said whispering grass, (laughter), didn't any of them move off the bandstand. They no fighters, no heart for fighting. Clyde Heart's got his fingers and things to look out after, Buster Bailey has got his embouchure and his fingers to look out after. So they ain't going to fight nothing. (Laughter). So about two weeks later, I get a summons to appear in court. Well the court that I had to go to was right up underneath the House of (Eden?) which is a ladies jail. I'd say around 14th Street in the Village.
